name: Methandriol

lead: Methandriol (methylandrostenediol) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid developed by Organon, active by mouth or injection. It is a 17-alpha-methylated derivative of androstenediol and is structurally close to methyltestosterone.

For appearance it belongs to the muscle-building category: anabolic steroids raise muscle size and leanness, and methandriol was historically sold for that purpose as well as for medical use in breast cancer.

paras: Historically it was marketed as aqueous injectable suspensions under names such as Androteston M, Notandron and Protandren. Today it is described mainly in bodybuilding and doping literature, and is detected in anti-doping testing.

As an anabolic-androgenic steroid it is a controlled substance in many countries and has virilizing effects in women. It remains marketed for clinical use only in Taiwan and for veterinary use in Australia.

chain: Greater muscle mass and leaner physique
angle.text: Methandriol is an anabolic steroid, so its place in appearance is muscle size and leanness. It is a historical product rather than a current mainstream one.

lead: Methandriol, also called methylandrostenediol, is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid developed by Organon. It was first synthesised in 1935 alongside methyltestosterone and mestanolone and was studied in breast cancer in the early 1950s [1].

Its appearance relevance is muscle: like other anabolic-androgenic steroids it is associated with gains in muscle mass, which is why it appears in bodybuilding and doping contexts. It is detected in anti-doping analysis in humans and racehorses [2][3].
Published research is mostly analytical: methods to detect methandriol and related 17-alpha-alkyl steroids in horses and in illicit products [2][3].
infobox: Controlled in many countries; clinical use only in Taiwan

paras: Methandriol was used to treat breast cancer in women; at comparable doses it was reported to be almost as virilizing as testosterone propionate and methyltestosterone [1].
Anabolic-androgenic steroids as a class are used for physique goals, and methandriol is classified with them in doping and detection literature [3]. Specific use data for methandriol are limited.
It is an orally active 17-alpha-alkylated androstane steroid, a derivative of androstenediol, with esters including dipropionate, propionate and bisenanthoyl acetate [1].
The main documented effect in women is virilization [1]. Anabolic steroids as a class are controlled substances because of misuse concerns [3].

Brazil lists it as a Class C5 anabolic steroid. It is clinically marketed only in Taiwan and as a veterinary product in Australia. Brand names include Anabol, Cytobolin, Diandren, Durabolic, Madiol and Stenediol [1].

A 2008 study identified urinary metabolites shared by methandienone, methandriol and oxymetholone in horses to support doping tests [2], and a 2025 Raman spectroscopy method detected methandriol among four illicitly added steroids in food and drug products [3].
No studies found on methandriol for muscle or appearance. Historic breast cancer studies date to the early 1950s [1].
